description:
DAYS NOTICE OF FELLING OF DANGEROUS LIME TREE T36. The stumps of trees T23 and T36 will be ground out and within two years replacement young lime trees will be planted in place of T23 and T36 as required for felled TPO trees,
The reasons for felling T36 are because the lower trunk was observed by a Management Company Director swaying noticeably in the storm so its anchor roots may be damaged like T23 that blew down, it has large areas of decay visible at the base (see photo in attachment B), there is a large old wound at about 3 m that has a large cavity with decay visible (see photo) which the tree surgeon advised is very likely hollow to the base, the tree trunk above the cavity was observed swaying to a significantly greater extent in the storm, and the tree's growth is heavily weighted towards the nearby building (see photo)
application_type_full: Tree works: Trees in conservation areas/subject to TPOs
decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - This consent is valid for a period of two years and does not authorise any works carried out beyond that period.
Reason: In accordance with the Town and Country Planning (Tree Preservation) (England) Regulations 2012.

Condition : 2 - A 2m high replacement tree of the same species, is to be planted in the same location, in the first available planting season following the removal of the tree hereby permitted, unless a variation to this is agreed in writing with the local planning authority.  Confirmation when planting has taken place should be sent to trees@wandsworth.gov.uk 
Reason: To preserve the visual amenity of the area in accordance with Planning Practice Guidance on Tree Preservation Orders and to safeguard the appearance of the locality, in accordance with Council policy LP56 of the Local Plan.
